title: Kimchi Jjigae
subtitle: Korean pork and kimchi stew
excerpt: This recipe approximates kimchi jjigae using fresh cabbage seasoned with gochugaru and a splash of vinegar, which gives the necessary acidity without requiring properly fermented kimchi. If you have access to aged, sour kimchi, use 300 g of it in place of the cabbage, gochugaru, and vinegar.
sourceNotes: Kimchi jjigae is considered a Korean comfort food staple, made from aged kimchi -- the sourer the better -- simmered with pork and a robust amount of gochugaru. In its authentic form the dish uses kimchi that has fermented for several weeks; this version substitutes fresh spiced cabbage.

content.text: Pork belly suits this stew because the fat renders slowly into the broth, giving the soup its characteristic richness. Do not trim the fat before cooking. If you have aged, sour kimchi to hand, use 300 g of it in place of the cabbage, gochugaru, and white wine vinegar.

items.prepNote: adds tang to approximate fermented kimchi

content.text: Toss the shredded cabbage with the gochugaru and white wine vinegar and set aside.
Heat the sesame oil in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the pork belly and cook for 5 minutes until the fat has started to render and the edges are slightly browned.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute. Add the gochujang and stir to coat the pork. Cook for 1 minute more.
Add the spiced cabbage and stir. Pour in the chicken stock and bring to a simmer. Add the soy sauce.
Simmer uncovered for 25 minutes until the pork is tender and the broth is deeply red and savoury. Add the spring onion for the last 2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning.

items.cause: Gochugaru and gochujang vary in heat between brands.
items.fix: Add another half tablespoon of gochugaru at the end and simmer for 2 minutes. Taste before adding more.

items.symptom: Pork belly still firm and chewy.
items.fix: Simmer for an extra 10-15 minutes. The pork should be soft enough to break with a spoon.
